children: has settled a long-running Justice Department lawsuit accusing its pharmacies of improperly dispensing opioids, removing a potentially multibillion-dollar legal overhang that has followed the retailer since 2020. Financial terms were not disclosed, limiting investors' ability to immediately quantify the cost, but the resolution reduces uncertainty around one of Walmart's most significant remaining opioid cases.

The federal government alleged Walmart pharmacies repeatedly violated the Controlled Substances Act by dispensing opioid prescriptions despite warning signs that some prescriptions were invalid. The case was among the Justice Department's major corporate enforcement actions tied to the U.S. opioid crisis and had exposed Walmart to potentially billions of dollars in penalties.

"The department is pleased to have reached a settlement with Walmart resolving allegations that its pharmacies failed to comply ?with their obligations under the Controlled Substances Act in dispensing opioids and other controlled substances," a Justice Department spokesperson told Reuters.

The settlement follows years of litigation. A federal judge narrowed portions of the government's case in 2024 but allowed important claims to proceed. Walmart and the government have now filed a joint stipulation seeking dismissal of the case. Walmart shares rose about 0.5% following the news.
This is not Walmart's first major opioid resolution. The retailer agreed in 2022 to pay
to resolve thousands of lawsuits brought by state and local governments alleging its pharmacies contributed to the opioid epidemic.

The federal settlement removes an important legal uncertainty, but investors should not treat it as the end of Walmart's opioid exposure. The company disclosed in its latest annual filing that several opioid-related cases remain pending in federal and state courts, including cases involving healthcare providers, third-party payers and individuals. The biggest near-term question is the undisclosed settlement cost and whether Walmart records any material charge. Beyond that, investors should watch remaining litigation and legal reserves, although these risks are unlikely to outweigh Walmart's core earnings drivers unless additional large settlements emerge.

title: Walmart Closes Difficult Chapter With High-Stakes Move
